title: RAGLabs: Build a RAG Pipeline, Then Measure Why It Fails
summary: An open-source workbench for retrieval-augmented generation. Upload documents, build and tune every stage of the pipeline from a web UI, chat with cited answers, then score the pipeline on questions generated from your own documents, with a diagnosis for every miss.
details: Most RAG failures happen before the LLM writes a word: the right passage was never retrieved. RAGLabs makes that measurable.
No-code pipeline: parse, chunk, embed, store, retrieve, rerank, prompt and generate, each with real options. Every saved configuration is an immutable version you can diff and roll back to.

Retrieval: dense, BM25 keyword, hybrid and fused search with exact matching for error messages and code symbols; RRF or weighted fusion, MMR, query expansion (multi-query, HyDE) and local cross-encoder reranking.
Vector stores behind one contract and one shared test suite: NumPy, FAISS (Flat, IVF, HNSW), Chroma, Qdrant and LanceDB. Switching store never re-embeds.
Evaluation: one-click eval sets from your documents; Hit@k, MRR, nDCG, tokens and p50/p95 latency, optional LLM-graded answers with 95% confidence intervals.
Sweeps over up to 4 settings with a quality-vs-cost Pareto leaderboard; Promote makes the winner live.
Corpus Health turns real user questions into a backlog of what the documents can't answer, plus duplicates, contradictions and stale documents.
Bring your own RAG: score any HTTP endpoint or Python function on the same eval set, and gate CI with the raglabs CLI.
Runs locally: documents and indexes stay in SQLite and a local vector store; API keys are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.

On a 13-question set from the Pydantic v2 docs demo, a tuned configuration ranked the right passage first 77% of the time (Hit@1) and in the top 3 every time. That set is small and generated from the same documents, so it is a smoke test, not a benchmark.

title: Network Intrusion Detection on KDD99
summary: Classifies network traffic as normal or one of four attack types, with SMOTE and One-vs-Rest models to catch the rarest attacks. A second stage experiments with predicting CVSS severity from CVE data.
details: Two-stage pipeline: intrusion detection on KDD99, then CVSS severity prediction on CVE data.
Random Forest and XGBoost ensembles; overall accuracy ~99%, but KDD99 is dominated by easy DoS traffic, so per-class F1 is the more honest measure.
Binary One-vs-Rest models with SMOTE: F1 of 99.9% Normal, 100% DoS, 99.2% Probe, 95.3% R2L and 64% U2R.
SMOTE was applied after the train/test split, to the training data only (35 U2R samples oversampled to 330,959).
The test set has only 17 U2R samples. SMOTE raised U2R recall from 6 of 17 (35%) to 8 of 17 (47%), with 100% precision.

Stage 2 predicts a CVSS score from 0 to 10 with regression (R² ≈ 0.98), but its 21 features include the six CVSS v2 access and impact metrics the score is calculated from, so that R² mostly reflects the formula rather than real prediction.

title: Portfolio AI Twin: Grounded Chat Assistant
summary: The chat assistant on this page. It answers questions about my work using only this site's content, cites the section each answer came from, and says when it doesn't know.
details: The page and the assistant read the same data files, so they can't disagree. A build step turns them into a tagged context pack and fails if it goes over 8,000 tokens or contains a phone number.
The model cites block IDs; the server strips them out and sends them as source chips that scroll to the matching section.
Input rules decline salary, politics, personal and prompt-injection questions without calling the model. An output check stops phone numbers and prompt leaks mid-stream.
Rate limits of 20 requests per 10 minutes per visitor (salted IP hash) and 500 a day overall. Logs keep only the question, topic, latency and outcome, and expire after 90 days.
70 eval cases (facts, multi-hop, unknowns, out-of-scope, prompt injection, PII) run against each deployment. Gates: 95% overall, 100% on injection, PII and out-of-scope.

title: Symbio-NLM: AI-Powered DNA Insight & Summary Platform
summary: A genomics web app that analyzes DNA sequences and explains them in plain language. The backend does the sequence analysis; Gemini writes the summaries and powers a chat assistant.
details: Backend processing for GC-content analysis, ORF detection, nucleotide distribution and FASTA validation.
Gemini AI APIs for sequence-specific natural-language summaries and chatbot-based genomics help.
Animated AI assistant chatbot with contextual interactions, built with GSAP.
REST API with JWT and bcrypt authentication.
